chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about one who confessed to his heirs that a debt was upon him while he was ill. He said: "What he confessed to is valid if it is small."

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a debt or right
key_terms.مَرِيض: The ill person (specifically in the context of deathbed or final illness)

ai.seo_question: Is a debt confession made by a dying person valid if the amount is small?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Samaa’ah reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validated a debt confession made during illness only if the amount was small, reflecting the juristic concern that large confessions might be fabricated to favor specific heirs. This ruling highlights the Shia legal principle of distinguishing between genuine acknowledgment and potential strategic disposition of wealth (*mugharrarah*) when a person is near death, ensuring fairness in inheritance distribution.
